text: To draw a segment of a circle, accepting an angle equal to a given rectilinear angle, on a given straight-line. Let $AB$ be the given straight-line, and $C$ the given rectilinear angle. So it is required to draw a segment of a circle, accepting an angle equal to $C$, on the given straight-line $AB$. So the [angle] $C$ is surely either acute, a right-angle, or obtuse. First of all, let it be acute.
And, as in the first diagram (from the left), let (angle) $BAD$, equal to angle $C$, be constructed on the straight-line $AB$, at the point A (on it) [Prop.~1.23].
Thus, $BAD$ is also acute.
Let $AE$ be drawn, at right-angles to $DA$ [Prop.~1.11].
And let $AB$ be cut in half at $F$ [Prop.~1.10].
And let $FG$ be drawn from point $F$, at right-angles to $AB$ [Prop.~1.11].
And let $GB$ be joined.
And since $AF$ is equal to $FB$, and $FG$ (is) common, the two (straight-lines) $AF$, $FG$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $BF$, $FG$ (respectively).

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the two (straight-lines) $AF$, $FG$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $BF$, $FG$ (respectively)

text: And angle $AFG$ (is) equal to [angle] $BFG$.
Thus, the base $AG$ is equal to the base $BG$ [Prop.~1.4].

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: base $AG$ is equal to the base $BG$

text: Thus, the circle drawn with center $G$, and radius $GA$, will also go through $B$ (as well as $A$).
assertion: circle with center G radius GA passes through both A and B

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the circle drawn with center $G$, and radius $GA$, will also go through $B$ (as well as $A$)

text: Let it be drawn, and let it be (denoted) $ABE$.
And let $EB$ be joined.
Therefore, since $AD$ is at the extremity of diameter $AE$, (namely, point) $A$, at right-angles to $AE$, the (straight-line) $AD$ thus touches the circle $ABE$ [Prop.~3.16~corr.].

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: $AD$ is at the extremity of diameter $AE$, (namely, point) $A$, at right-angles to $AE$

text: Therefore, since some straight-line $AD$ touches the circle $ABE$, and some (other) straight-line $AB$ has been drawn across from the point of contact $A$ into circle $ABE$, angle $DAB$ is thus equal to the angle $AEB$ in the alternate segment of the circle [Prop.~3.32].
assertion: angle DAB equals angle AEB in the alternate segment

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: some (other) straight-line $AB$ has been drawn across from the point of contact $A$ into circle $ABE$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: angle $DAB$ is thus equal to the angle $AEB$ in the alternate segment of the circle

text: But, $DAB$ is equal to $C$.
Thus, angle $C$ is also equal to $AEB$.
Thus, a segment $AEB$ of a circle, accepting the angle $AEB$ (which is) equal to the given (angle) $C$, has been drawn on the given straight-line $AB$.
assertion: segment AEB accepting angle equal to C has been drawn on AB (case 1: acute)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: a segment $AEB$ of a circle, accepting the angle $AEB$ (which is) equal to the given (angle) $C$, has been drawn on the given straight-line $AB$

text: And so let $C$ be a right-angle. And let it again be necessary to draw a segment of a circle on $AB$, accepting an angle equal to the right-[angle] $C$.
Let the (angle) $BAD$ [again] be constructed, equal to the right-angle $C$ [Prop.~1.23], as in the second diagram (from the left).
And let $AB$ be cut in half at $F$ [Prop.~1.10].
And let the circle $AEB$ be drawn with center $F$, and radius either $FA$ or $FB$.
Thus, the straight-line $AD$ touches the circle $ABE$, on account of the angle at $A$ being a right-angle [Prop.~3.16 corr.].

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: the angle at $A$ being a right-angle

text: And angle $BAD$ is equal to the angle in segment $AEB$. For (the latter angle), being in a semi-circle, is also a right-angle [Prop.~3.31].
assertion: angle BAD equals angle in segment AEB

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: angle $BAD$ is equal to the angle in segment $AEB$

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: (the latter angle), being in a semi-circle, is also a right-angle

text: But, $BAD$ is also equal to $C$.
Thus, the (angle) in (segment) $AEB$ is also equal to $C$.
assertion: angle in segment AEB equals C

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the (angle) in (segment) $AEB$ is also equal to $C$

text: Thus, a segment $AEB$ of a circle, accepting an angle equal to $C$, has again been drawn on $AB$.
assertion: segment AEB accepting angle equal to C has been drawn on AB (case 2: right-angle)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: a segment $AEB$ of a circle, accepting an angle equal to $C$, has again been drawn on $AB$

text: And so let (angle) $C$ be obtuse.
And let (angle) $BAD$, equal to ($C$), be constructed on the straight-line $AB$, at the point $A$ (on it) [Prop.~1.23], as in the third diagram (from the left).
And let $AE$ be drawn, at right-angles to $AD$ [Prop.~1.11].
And let $AB$ again be cut in half at $F$ [Prop.~1.10].
And let $FG$ be drawn, at right-angles to $AB$ [Prop.~1.10].
And let $GB$ be joined.
And again, since $AF$ is equal to $FB$, and $FG$ (is) common, the two (straight-lines) $AF$, $FG$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $BF$, $FG$ (respectively).

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the two (straight-lines) $AF$, $FG$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $BF$, $FG$ (respectively)

text: And angle $AFG$ (is) equal to angle $BFG$.
Thus, the base $AG$ is equal to the base $BG$ [Prop.~1.4].

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: base $AG$ is equal to the base $BG$

text: Thus, a circle of center $G$, and radius $GA$, being drawn, will also go through $B$ (as well as $A$).
assertion: circle with center G radius GA passes through both A and B (case 3)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: a circle of center $G$, and radius $GA$, being drawn, will also go through $B$ (as well as $A$)

text: Let it go like $AEB$ (in the third diagram from the left).
And since $AD$ is at right-angles to the diameter $AE$, at its extremity, $AD$ thus touches circle $AEB$ [Prop.~3.16~corr.].

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: $AD$ is at right-angles to the diameter $AE$, at its extremity

text: And $AB$ has been drawn across (the circle) from the point of contact $A$. Thus, angle $BAD$ is equal to the angle constructed in the alternate segment $AHB$ of the circle [Prop.~3.32].
assertion: angle BAD equals angle in alternate segment AHB

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: $AB$ has been drawn across (the circle) from the point of contact $A$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: angle $BAD$ is equal to the angle constructed in the alternate segment $AHB$ of the circle

text: But, angle $BAD$ is equal to $C$.
Thus, the angle in segment $AHB$ is also equal to $C$.
assertion: angle in segment AHB equals C

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the angle in segment $AHB$ is also equal to $C$

text: Thus, a segment $AHB$ of a circle, accepting an angle equal to $C$, has been drawn on the given straight-line $AB$.
assertion: segment AHB accepting angle equal to C has been drawn on AB (case 3: obtuse)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: a segment $AHB$ of a circle, accepting an angle equal to $C$, has been drawn on the given straight-line $AB$

text: (Which is) the very thing it was required to do.
